dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product shows the views its tabs switch between, under those tabs or apart from them, in a region that changes with the selection and that a person can swipe from view to view, the tabs' indicator following the finger, and decides once how far and how softly one view gives way to the next.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: Everything a Tab view reads for its panels: the corners that clip them (and that a focused panel's ring follows), the form a switch between two panels takes (a travel, a fade alone, or none), how the travel looks at its fullest (how far each panel travels, as a distance plus a share of the width of the region that holds them, how faded and how blurred it is), and the switch's motion, with and without reduced motion. The row of tabs a Tab view draws itself is a Tabs and reads the tabs' tokens, not these.
rules: By default a Tab view draws its own row of Tabs above its panels: give each panel its value and its tab's label (and an icon, on every panel or none), and set the row's variant, fullWidth and label on the Tab view.

When the tabs belong somewhere else (a top app bar, a sticky header), link the Tab view to that row (tabs) instead; it then draws no row, and its panels need only their values. Place it after that row in reading order, so that Tab moves from the selected tab into the panel.
One panel per tab, each with a unique value.
Restyle the Tab view's own row through the tabs' tokens, as any row of tabs; it is not a look-alike with tokens of its own.
Turn swiping off (swipeable false) when a panel is mostly content that is dragged sideways itself: a map, a drawing surface, a long horizontal chart.

motion.transition names the form of every switch, and the transition prop sets it for one view: slide is the travel the four transition values describe; fade is a crossfade alone; none shows the new panel in one frame, and the row the view draws then does not slide its indicator either. Choose none where the panels are read rather than watched (a code sample in several languages) and for a view that changes many times a minute.

The switch is one progress from 0 to 1: at 0 the old panel is at rest; at 1 it is transition.distance plus transition.distance-fraction of the width away, at transition.opacity and blurred by transition.blur, and the new panel is at rest. A distance-fraction of 1 with opacity 1 and blur 0 is a full-width page turn.
Keep motion.switch-duration and motion.switch-easing equal to the tabs' motion.indicator-duration and motion.indicator-easing, so that a tab's indicator and its panel land together.
Restyle through these tokens in a layer; never fork the component.

shape.$description: The corners of the region that holds the panels, below the Tab view's own row when it draws one. It clips a panel as it slides and blurs, and a focused panel's ring follows it. Square, because a Tab view usually spans the screen or its parent; a product that puts one inside a rounded surface rounds it.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product decides once how its views give way to each other when a tab or a swipe switches them: a short shift that softens and fades (the default), a full page turn that follows the finger, or a plain crossfade. The four values together are the switch at its fullest; the progress between rest and fullest is the component's.

distance.$description: How far a panel travels between rest and the fullest point of a switch, before distance-fraction adds a share of the Tab view's width. The old panel moves this far toward the side it leaves by; the new one starts this far away on the other side.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: Material 3's tab content is a pager: it travels a whole width (distance-fraction 1) and nothing more.

distance-fraction.$description: The share of the Tab view's width added to distance: 0 keeps the travel at distance whatever the width; 1 (with distance 0) makes the panels travel a whole width, so that they move with the finger and meet edge to edge, as a page turn does.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: Material 3 swipes tab content as pages that follow the finger and meet edge to edge.

opacity.$description: A panel's opacity at the fullest point of a switch: the old panel fades to it as it leaves, the new one fades from it as it arrives. 0 is a crossfade; 1 draws no fade.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: Material 3's pages do not fade as they slide.

blur.$description: How blurred a panel is at the fullest point of a switch: the standard deviation of the Gaussian, as the web's filter: blur() takes it. A platform whose blur takes another quantity converts; it never passes the number through. 0 draws no blur.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: Material 3's pages are not blurred as they slide.

transition.$description: The form a switch between two panels takes in a Tab view whose transition the product did not set (TBV-22). slide: the panels travel, fade and blur as transition.distance, transition.distance-fraction, transition.opacity and transition.blur say, over switch-duration, and follow a swipe. fade: the two panels crossfade in place over fade-duration, and crossfade with a swipe. none: the new panel is shown whole in the frame the selection is made, a swipe moves nothing before its release, and the row the view draws puts its indicator on the new tab at once. Reduced motion draws slide as fade and never adds motion to fade or none. The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product decides once whether its views travel, crossfade or simply change when a tab is chosen, and still sets one view apart: a code sample whose panels are read, not watched, changes at once in a product whose screens otherwise travel.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: A choice of kind; no dial scales it.

switch-duration.$description: How long a switch takes when a tab is selected, and how long the rest of it takes after a swipe is released. The tabs' indicator slides over the same default, so the two land together.

switch-easing.$description: The switch's easing. A spatial spring may overshoot; the travel follows it, the fade and the blur stop at their end points.

fade-duration.$description: Where motion is reduced, how long the crossfade that replaces the switch takes.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: Where motion is reduced the travel and the blur are dropped and only a fade is left; one product times that fade apart from the switch, which is spatial and longer.

fade-easing.$description: The reduced-motion crossfade's easing: the curve of a change of state, which never overshoots.
